Recent advances in linear transport methods, including OSN and P3, have shown a promising fit with equilibrium data on lipid bilayers. However, these models predict properties that contradict equilibrium measurements for certain bilayer components. This discrepancy arises due to artificial, thermodynamically impossible equilibria created during the linearization process, affecting membrane components in fixed association with lipids. To address this issue, we have modified the OSN model to incorporate a equilibrium constraint, combining bilayer and associated component equilibria. Applying Flory-Huggins statistics to coupled components resolved this previously noted imbalance. Furthermore, we have reformulated the P3 model to remove nonphysical constraints. This revised theory maintains physical n-alkane chain pseudocapacities similar to the original OSN but eliminates the discrepancies associated with associated components. To validate our findings, we have analyzed the experimentally determined parameter values for C16/20/22 PEG-lipid bilayers and compared them to predictions made by the revised model, showing a positive outcome.

An alternative method to quantum cosmology is proposed by utilizing a modified Friedmann equation derived from loop quantum gravity and tested with Big Bang Model simulations.  Although the new model shares some similarities with other loop quantum gravity-based cosmological models, it possesses a critical bounce density half that of the APS LQC model and requires less than twice the critical bounce density to initiate bounce.  Additionally, a quantum phase transition occurs at a density below the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis density at which certain particles are formed, without the necessity of a dynamic triangulation number and without violating the BBN principle.  Interestingly, the model agrees with the COBE data and WMAP data for certain values of the matter energy density when considered within the context of the standard Big Bang model.  Furthermore, the model's predictions for certain parameters, including the deceleration parameter and parameters related to the acceleration of the universe, are constrained by analyzing the gold data from supernovae type Ia, suggesting that the universe is currently in a phase of weak acceleration.  Overall, the model provides an adequate explanation for various observational evidence including the flatness and homogeneity of the universe as well as its late-stage enterability into the De Sitter phase.

The Antarctic Air Shower Observatory, ANTARES, has been operating a multigazion muon telescope in Antarctica since 2014, aiming to verify predictions about the highest-energy cosmic rays. A new findings publication presents over 99 extensive air showers observed by the telescope, focusing on those with the highest energy, all of which featured multiple muons detected as far as 240 meters from the primary interaction site. A comprehensive catalog of these showers has been compiled, featuring detailed information on primary energy estimates, signals from each detector, track lengths, and muon densities. Additionally, the research describes a new method for locating the observation point of each shower, notes a discrepancy in primary energy estimates between their own model and a established formula, and fails to confirm certain expectations about the morphology of these showers.

Accurate object detection and uncertainty calculation depend on accurate bounding box (bx) prediction and corner estimation. Current object detection methods focus on improving bounding box prediction but often neglect corner estimation. We introduce BayesOD, a novel, end-to-end object detection method utilizing yellowdots to represent object corners and calculate uncertainty. BayesOD incorporates a corner estimation process with yellowdots, an efficient representation of corner locations and uncertainties. This approach integrates Dixon mixing and stochastic mapping for improved yellowdot propagation, simulation, and estimation. Performance metrics reveal BayesOD achieving high accuracy, deep, and uncertain bounding box predictions with high mean auROC values, an increased mean auPRC of 0.10 compared to Faster R-CNN, and a more consistent performance across different datasets. The method's source code is available at $\ur<https://github.com/Amkhan18/2022_arXiv_2209.04053/blob/main/code/2022_arXiv_2209.04053.od.zip>

This research presents UnoNet, a UNet-based architecture expansion, named UnoNet,
especially suitable for traffic forecasting and other tasks requiring real-time
forecasting of spatio-temporal sequences. From the perspective of architectural
progression, we start with the basic Unet, then add the parallel connection of
parallel convolutions and expansion- compression block. Furthermore, we introduce
UnoNet, consisting of a feature extraction convolutional encoder and a decoding
convolutional-deconvolutional block series, complemented by parallel convolutions,
expansion-compression block series, and soft-one gate, aimed at producing a
sequence of forecasted values rather than mere traffic flow. Both UnoNet and
its progressive architecture UnoNet have exhibited superior performance in the
prediction of traffic volume and other metrics for spatio-temporal sequence
prediction, such as graph-based traffic flow and missing video frame prediction
tasks. In experiments, UnoNet has outperformed the relevant baselines on the
extended dataset of Chongqing and MUST, with further detailed analysis of its
progressive architecture and the related source code provided online at a
designated URL.

This paper expands the concept of a rewriting system, which was initially defined for precategories in a previous work, to a specific new context. This expanded concept is then used to develop coherent substitution systems, coarsest rewrite paths, and stable precategories. It also provides lemmas that help prove precategoral consistency, allowing for a consistency-based definition of parallel and choice combiners. Building upon these results, the paper develops a framework for combining parallel and choice operators within and across different rewriting systems, while maintaining consistency. Lastly, the paper illustrates the utility of this framework with concrete examples from the fields of algebra and rewriting.

Automatic segmentation of the hippocampus has significant applications for quantifying hippocampus at risk and volumetric changes. Past studies have investigated the performance of automated segmentation methods, but they largely relied on data from healthy individuals and individuals with temporal lobe epilepsy. There is a lack of research on the performance of these methods in diverse populations, including those with small to large hippocampus resections. This study differs from previous ones by utilizing a large dataset comprising 331 patients who have undergone open surgery for hippocampus resection at five institutions across the globe. The dataset was created in partnership with the HIPSEIZURE consortium and includes mesial temporal lobe epilepsy patients alongside healthy individuals. The accuracy of various state-of-the-art hippocampus segmentation methods was evaluated on this new dataset using a recently proposed metric that takes into account both false positive and false negative volumes. The results show that while the performance of SPM is comparable to that of deep learning methods, such as ValenceNet and Hippocampal90, in healthy individuals and patients with temporal lobe epilepsy, these methods exhibit substantially decreased accuracy in patients who have undergone open surgery for hippocampus resection. The formation of false clusters from false positive voxels is identified as a key factor contributing to the decreased accuracy, particularly those with larger resections.

We introduce a class of quantum experiments that integrates path and traversal dimensions. A key feature of these experiments is that path dimensions are coupled to traversal degrees of freedom through transversal modes. The feasibility of conducting such experiments relies on creating transversal entanglement between paths and trajectories. Upon retrieving the original path dimensions, we find that they remain unchanged due to a unique decoherence mechanism, allowing distillated information to resist environmental influence. This theoretical framework facilitates the assessment of experiments that claim non-locality and may imply the implementation of non-standard interferometers, including those potentially emerging from investigations of gravitational phenomena.

The atmospheric cosmic ray component is generated through interactions of high-energy cosmic rays with the Earth's atmosphere, producing secondary and tertiary cosmic rays. Protons up to a few trillion TeV are created during this process, serving as cosmic ray sources. These source protons then participate in further cosmic ray interactions, whereas observed cosmic rays, detected at Earth, are primarily generated outside the solar system. Our analysis examines the atmospheric cosmic ray proportion originating from source protons, whereas existing literature focuses on tertiary cosmic rays and their corresponding spatial distribution. To achieve this, two techniques are employed: a Monte Carlo simulation based on a simplified atmospheric model with uniform horizontal and vertical projection, and an analytical model using the Boltzmann transport equation. Our simulations yield complementary results that correlate well with each other, and our findings suggest that the atmospheric cosmic ray proportion originating from source protons exceeds 90%.

Recent studies have shown that a pyramidal-like skeleton offers several benefits, 
such as increased flexibility in data parallel training and reduced data loss 
due to dropout. However, this skeleton is difficult to implement in certain 
deep learning models, particularly those using a linear layer for embedding 
transformation in Transformer architectures. In this research, we propose a new 
approach using Skipped-attention-Transformer (SAT) to efficiently utilize the 
pyramidal-like skeleton effectively. The SAT model aggregates information from 
spatial and temporal aspects using two parallel networks, one for spatial 
aggregation and the other for temporal aggregation. We applied this model to 
two prominent benchmarks, Speech-Transformer for speech classification and Image- 
Transformer for image classification, and implemented it in a way that mimics the 
Skipped-attention-plot of a pyramidal skeleton through token dropping and skip 
connections, thereby fulfilling its inherent properties. Furthermore, our model 
can also be viewed as a novel method for efficient data-parallel training. We 
believe that SAT offers a valuable strategy for designing more efficient and 
scalable Transformer models.

This research proposes a new differential privacy mechanism, known as the Huber mechanism, which is based on a Gaussian process and aims to provide a more context-free approach to differential privacy. Mechanization of this process involves applying a Gaussian process based on a distance metric to protect individual data. The study evaluates the differential privacy properties of the Huber mechanism and compares its results to those of the Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms. The findings show that the Huber mechanism achieves a reasonable balance between differential privacy and utility while also providing an alternative to the Gaussian mechanism, which is suitable for applications requiring a more context-free approach to differential privacy.

The far-infrared polarization observed from 0.4 to 0.8 mm in this study, using ARIE on the submillimeter wing of the Subaru telescope, did not show any frequency dependence that could be expected based on the optical properties of perfectly aligned non-spherical grains of uniform size. This leads to the conclusion that large interstellar dust grains are not exclusively composed of carbon. Additionally, the non-variability of the observed polarization angle over a 30 arcsecond range, within this frequency range, suggests a single scattering event plays the main role in far-infrared polarization observed in the interstellar medium. However, the possibility of the signal originating from our own Galaxy cannot be ruled out. A comparison of the observed polarization and temperature ratios suggests a minimal impact of radiative transfer effects on far-infrared polarization signal in the interstellar medium.

A substantial, Jupiter-like planet may be present in the disk $DOB-82$, as suggested by submillimeter emission features. This paper presents an analysis of dust and gas emission in a section of the disk influenced by a potential planet, using millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths. Millimeter observations of CO molecules indicate a lack of density, while submillimeter observations of dust show an unusual pattern. This paper explores two scenarios - a ring-like structure caused by a planet's gravitational influence, and a disk with uneven CO density, to explain the CO and dust emission patterns. Both scenarios fit the observations, but the ring-like structure better explains the submillimeter dust emission pattern. If a planet is present, its mass is estimated to be similar to that of Jupiter, and it orbits the host every 1.57 days.

The "Most Clicks Problem" involves determining which element from a strategically placed group of $k$ clicks will receive the $i^{th}$ click on a $d$-dimensional grid, where $d$ is greater than or equal to $3$. The optimal strategy for this problem has been previously established, resulting in the best-known lower bound for its solution complexity. The problem's complexity lower bound is directly tied to the nullity of a specific, related combinatorial structure, specifically $\lambda_{\Lambda}(d,k)$, in the context of multilinear forms. The key contribution of this work is in proving a new complexity lower bound for MCP by demonstrating the existence of a family of forms with nullity greater than or equal to $k^{\left\lceil \frac{d}{2}
\right\rceil}$, providing an answer to an open question posed by the original MCP paper. The proof relies on a novel application of the Zarankiewicz lemma to establish a new complexity lower bound for this problem.

A modified piecewise constant Mumford-Shah model is suggested to segment images contaminated by non-overlapping, heavily masked areas. Diverging from traditional methods, the proposed approach aims to recover clean images rather than solely eliminating the noise. Initially, the model's first-order optimality conditions are identified and implemented using a dual-form algorithm combined with an alternating optimization technique. Through experimental validation, the proposed method's segmented clean image results are compared favorably against a prevailing approach. Moreover, the segmented clean images derived from the model demonstrate both practical applicability and effectiveness in restoring blurred images, a function beyond traditional piecewise constant multiphase segmentation algorithms.

Abstract interpretation, a top-down analysis method used in programming, has been enhanced with a new technique that allows for more accurate and detailed computed abstract error bounds, yielding tighter bounds and allowing for safer software-coded protection mechanisms against errors and failures. This method, founded on an abstract interpretation framework, offers improvements by factors of 5 to 27, demonstrating its superiority. The approach can be applied to a broad range of programming paradigms and is compatible with existing software, showcasing its potential for widespread adoption. The integration of abstract interpretation and depth analysis provides for a flexible and adaptable method that can be easily adapted to code written in script languages. This method, although primarily applicable to static analysis, has also been successfully applied to dynamic analysis, providing more accurate results. The development of tools, such as Verifast, and an example implementation, gnu-plot, illustrate the method's potential for use in a variety of scenarios, including safety-critical software coding for embedded devices.

This research focuses on the impact of ultra-violet (UV) irradiation on tetragonal CaTiO$_3$ perovskite in its high-temperature phase. By combining density functional theory and phonon analysis, it has been demonstrated that the high-temperature phase of CaTiO$_3$ exhibits topological phon modes similar to those found in Ca$_3$TiO$_3$. When excited by UV light, these modes develop a Chern number of -1, giving rise to a topological phon mode. Our results, supported by lattice dynamics calculations, show that the R-point phon mode transforms from nodal-linking to gapped, and further changes to a non-zero Chern number mode. We have also proven that the Dirac phon mode merges with the topological phon mode, giving rise to a non-zero Chern number mode. Furthermore, it was found that the topological phon mode maintains its integrity even after returning to its original ground state, and only undergoes gapping when it interacts with other phon modes or structural changes.

This research introduces the MRPG (Multi-representation and Path-based clustering) algorithm for outlier identification, based on a novel geometric graph model. The MRPG + graph is constructed through a dynamic process incorporating multiple agent states, which facilitates efficient detection of outliers. Unlike conventional methods, MRPG eliminates the need for costly nearest neighbor search operations in each time step, thus increasing its detection efficiency. MRPG outperforms existing techniques, such as the Weighted Relative Neighborhood Search, by approximately 25% in detection speed, as demonstrated using random data sets. Furthermore, MRPG demonstrates its real-world application in clustering IoT device locations within mobile networks.

Neutral atoms moving near a perfectly reflecting mirror lose energy through a combination of photon emissions in left- and right-polarized states. Due to the mirror's reflection, these polarizations behave like their own independent two-level systems, which emit specific types of light. By comparing this effect with a system of two entangled atoms, researchers conclude that local realism cannot fully explain the predicted phenomenon, making it a potential source of quantum advantage in mirror-based atomic systems.

The graph representation learning field has extensively researched methods that extract node embeddings based on graph structure. Despite this focus, there has been limited exploration into the bias of these methods, specifically with regards to the fair learning paradigm. We build upon this understanding by examining the bias of graph representation learning. In our study, we delve into three key aspects: (1) We demonstrate that graph representation learning methods can learn and preserve latent node attributes in unbiased manners. (2) We detail a novel fair learning objective that utilises the latent node attributes to reduce bias in learning tasks, and enforce neighbourhood fairness as a form of regularisation. We find that this approach achieves significant improvements in both learning fairness and task performance, showcasing the importance of structural information in learning fairness. (3) We provide empirical evidence that popular graph representation learning methods, when operating in unfair environments, often result in reduced performance overall, regardless of the learning task in question. Interestingly, we find that neighbourhood fairness enforcement has a mixed effect on performance, with negative impact in some cases but positive in others, underscoring that graph structure should be leveraged in a targeted manner.

This research assessed the accuracy and computational speed of two approximate analytical techniques, the Homotopy Perturbation Method and Simple Iteration Method, for solving a nonlinear reversible enzyme reaction model under equilibrium and kinetic conditions. By comparing solutions from the two methods with exact numerical solutions and analytical exact solutions when applicable, it was found that the Homotopy Perturbation Method generally yielded more accurate results than the Simple Iteration Method but was also consistently outperformed by exact numerical solutions. When comparing the Homotopy Perturbation Method with the Simple Iteration Method, it was observed that while both methods could approximate the model's equilibrium state with reasonable accuracy, the Simple Iteration Method was noticeably faster to compute. Given these findings, it is suggested that the Simple Iteration Method may be a suitable choice for initial guess generation in models where the Homotopy Perturbation Method is not feasible due to its increased computational demands.

A novel search strategy for discovering long-lived gluinos at the Large Hadron Collider was developed, focusing on gluino decays with short ranges rather than their full disintegration. By utilizing specialized reconstruction and assignment procedures, the new approach efficiently identified final products of gluino collapses in jet clusters. The search was carried out not only in the directions of particles' disappearance but also in the locations of their disappearance, yielding more sensitive gluino discovery capabilities, especially for masses exceeding 2 TeV, where life spans of gluinos are considerable and detection challenging. The search did not yield an anomaly and resulted in limits on the gluino's mass and decay length, specifically, its minimum values were 2.5 TeV with a decay length of 10 cm and 3.0 TeV with a decay length of 50 cm. The new search revealed enhanced sensitivity in the detection of gluino decays with short ranges and served as an effective supplement to existing searches which primarily targeted comprehensive gluino disintegration.

A decentralized trading system with limitless wealth is presented, in which a network of agents engages in a one-shot trade. Each agent initially chooses a supplier, and subsequently chooses to buy or sell the good from their selected supplier through a binary decision. The decision to buy or sell is made by a strategy that prioritizes expected returns from each option. The system's market equilibrium is reached at a distribution of buyer/seller choices, and results are shown for two key measures - the market output size and the output distribution's standard deviation. The findings are compared to a strategy that relies solely on expectations, and it's shown that market feedback that breaks even and incurs loss can lead to the collapse of financial bubbles more quickly. The findings are also extended to a scenario with multiple rounds of trade, and it's found that while unimodal market output size distributions can become more symmetrical over many rounds of trade, the market may still be characterized by significant volatility. The system's excess volatility can be explained by the presence of early-round 'irrational' traders who adopt strategies that incur losses, and the traders' preference for early-round 'rational' strategies that incur losses for these 'irrational' traders in return for higher expected returns from 'rational' traders' strategic behavior.

A single photon drive is implemented on the XY model's quantum critical interface in 2D with Ising spins. This drives an intense, synchronized state of states within the interface's boundary. The driven system's long-term state exhibits multiple, distinct phase states, each associated with a different pattern of states. The interface's driven states bridge two main phase states, reducing their disparity, and a smaller distance separates the two states in a'sandwich' pattern. The driven states show a common thread - all exhibit suppressed entanglement and order. The driven states' probability distribution is found to have minimal entanglement. The driven states' probability distribution is found to have minimal entanglement. This is a simplified model for a multi-photon experiment seeking a multi-photon subspace in a system with a large number of coupled oscillators.

Modular review formats consisting of a textual description and interactive elements like stars, photos, and dates enable reviewers to convey information more efficiently. However, current text-based recommendation models overlook these interactive elements when making predictions. As these elements convey reviewers' opinions more explicitly, incorporating them into text representations could lead to enhanced prediction accuracy. This paper demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating interactive features into text representations and proposes a novel model called IFRM, which combines the strengths of both text and interactive feature-based recommendation models. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of IFRM over existing approaches in achieving better prediction performance.

Generating CS data automatically using existing code-mixing data is a great way to augment limited datasets programatically. Current methods though, only replace individual words at a time from one language's sentence to another, which may not preserve enough information. This paper proposes an innovative method called CS-AR for augmenting data programatically where instead of individual words, longer segments get replaced, this way preserving more useful info from the source sentence. The CS-AR method uses archive data in a specific order to produce new data with a particular structure. During experimentation using 5 major CS language pairs we found that, though programatic methods are not as accurate as supervised models, CS-AR outperformed existing programatic methods and produced data that was better evaluated on 4 out of 5 metrics when compared to datasets produced using other programatic methods, leading to enhanced performance of up to 4.3 FLE. The study also confirmed the efficacy of the produced data from programatic methods for low resource environments, successfully cross-training a model to achieve up to $+6.2$ FLE compared to the baseline without extra data.

We establish equivalent definitions for the property of an embedded subgroup being topologically dense in a compact surface, and derive specific criteria for transitivity and precompactness in such surfaces. These criteria state that a subgroup's action on the surface's interior is topologically dense if and only if it is transitive or precompact on the surface as a whole. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for codimension-one subgroups, being topologically dense is equivalent to uniform density on the surface's boundary, and provide examples of subgroup structures for specific surfaces, namely the torus, Klein bottle, and double torus.

Brane placements in a background field which undergoes a transition from a background ultraviolet to infrared fixed point exhibit unique characteristics. At background fixed points, standard assumptions necessary for AdS/CFT correspondence are violated, resulting in non-trivial fluctuations for both the background and a brane embedded within it. We investigate Brane geometry deformations and their associated costs, focusing on both classical and quantum mechanical aspects. Research reveals a non-trivial fixed point phase diagram for a particular background, comprised of five-dimensional anti-de Sitter spaces featuring various numbers of minimal supersymmetric five-brane configurations. Furthermore, researchers discovered a connection between mass deformed N=6 superconformal quantum field theories and various brane arrangements in anti-de Sitter spaces.

The accuracy of computational mesh-based models heavily relies on the high quality of the mesh components. Malformed elements can severely impact results, necessitating the division of coarse elements into finer sub-elements when employing an Galerkin-based numerical approach. This process can greatly diminish the computational efficiency and effectiveness of the model. To mitigate these issues, element splitting is frequently used in conjunction with local mesh refinement techniques that optimize mesh elements. Despite existing knowledge on both methodologies being extensive, the literature lacks unified guidelines outlining the optimal implementation strategies for these methods. This research aims to bridge this knowledge gap by providing a comprehensive overview of common numerical methods and protocols for implementing both methodologies within the context of the standard 1D, 2D, and 3D finite element method formulation. To ensure the validity of our conclusions, we utilize a rigorous research framework comprising a systematic review of the literature, an analytical investigation of the merits and drawbacks of various methods, and an in-depth examination of the impact of different implementation details on the performance of these methods. We further report on the reliable and widely accepted best-practice standards for implementing mesh refinement via splitting and local refinement.

Knowledge graph link prediction focuses on forecasting link existence between entities in a knowledge graph. This study explores how relation extraction, a precursor to link prediction, benefits from its outcomes to enhance prediction performance. Three methods were developed to compare the quality of motion sensor data collection designed for link prediction with those annotated via relation extraction, finding the former to surpass the latter. Nevertheless, combining motion sensor data collection with relation extraction benefits link prediction. These findings suggest that motion sensor data can serve as a substitute for motion-based relation extraction, while integration of motion sensor data and relation extraction achieves superior link prediction outcomes than using either technique alone.

This research introduces an advanced analytical model for estimating electrical delays in MOSFET devices based on the strong-inversion framework. The proposed model's accuracy is evaluated and compared with established methods, including SPICE simulation, revealing that it achieves delays within 8% of predicted values. A practical example demonstrates how to integrate the model into the placement process to account for electrical delays when designing MOSFET devices.

Advanced reinforcement learning methods have extensive applications in high-impact domains, yet they are limited to discrete or finitely continuous state-action spaces. To overcome this challenge, a novel off-policy actor-critic algorithm is introduced in this research, which efficiently leverages approximate policy iteration to handle complex continuous spaces. Distinguishing it from existing algorithms, the new method employs a uniquely defined coarse graining metric that quantifies approximate policy representation. By incorporating this concept into the loss function of the target actor network, the algorithm enhances learning stability and convergence. Moreover, the introduction of temporal bootstrapping in the value network facilitates better handling of temporal correlations in the approximation error. The theoretical and experimental validations demonstrate the superior performance of the new method in a variety of continuous control scenarios.

Research in cognitive science focuses on understanding visual cues related to agency and animacy, identifying patterns or conditions that classify objects as active or inactive. Drawing from expertise in artificial life and visual representation, our research investigates how visual categorizability and agency independently affect our perception of animacy. Through a comprehensive study involving 250 subjects, we evaluated the visual characteristics of 60 images depicting various instances of animacy, such as robots and robots with wings, as well as inactive objects like rocks and clouds. By comparing human ratings of these images with the predictions of a state-of-the-art animacy detection network, our analysis reveals that visual categorizability and agency are distinct factors. While contributing significantly to the network's performance, agency has a more substantial impact on visual categorizability. Moreover, our research highlights that these cues operate along a continuum rather than a simple active or inactive classification. Furthermore, our study explores how these cues relate to more nuanced concepts, such as how animacy affects what is considered agency and what is part of the world.

A high-order spatial solver known as SPFilter has been implemented as an efficient numerical solution to partial differential equations, achieving optimal results in various fields including physics-informed scenarios. Due to its use of polynomial and series expansions that are tailored to capture boundary conditions and interior features, SPFilter generates inconsistent methods that are high in order, although it maintains consistency within the interior of the domain. In this work, a structure-preserving filter is introduced as an innovative post-processing technique that can be used in conjunction with various high-order spatial discretizations. This proposed method successfully addresses and rectifies the inconsistencies associated with polynomial-based simulations by enforcing a strong, sharp, and physically bound solution that adheres to boundary conditions. Additionally, the filtered solution has been theoretically analyzed and numerically tested with a series of numerical experiments that include interior and boundary state-driven problems, as well as multifrontal and multi-physical models like the Poisson and Burgers equations. These tests have consistently shown that FPFilter can successfully eliminate polynomial-based inconsistencies while maintaining a similar level of accuracy. Furthermore, FPFilter has been found to be particularly effective in capturing sharp frontiers and account for their proper propagation within the interior of the domain. In the case of physics-informed simulations, FPFilter has been found to enforce physically bound solutions that are in line with physical principles and, in turn, generates more accurate results. One of the notable advantages of FPFilter is that it can be used in conjunction with a wide range of high-order spatial discret

A black hole X-ray transient named GX394196 underwent an outburst in which various spectral patterns were observed, including the typical hard, soft and very high spectral states commonly found in these transients. This source displayed an unusual combination of type-C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) and heavy hydrogen absorption features across its various phases. In GX394196, a type-C QPO in the hard-intermediate state was distinguished by its high frequency. Furthermore, an exceptionally high frequency of 14.7 Hz type-C QPO was detected during the hard spectral state, whereas similar QPOs in GX394196 and GX3435-483 during their respective outbursts showed similar characteristics. In GX394196, another QPO type-A with a lower frequency than type-C was present, and could be explained as the result of Comptonisation of photons from the inner accretion flow. Measurements of the theory of shadow technique and the disc-tracker technique for GX394196's type-A QPO, yielded an accretion disk inner radius of approximately 11-16 km. In the very high spectral state, a type-C QPO with a frequency of 2.7 Hz was present, and could be explained as the result of the corona's free flow of photons over the curved accretion disk surface. Many multi-agent reinforcement learning systems struggle with efficiency and effectiveness, largely due to a shortage of useful data within their individual experiences. To tackle this challenge, we've developed the Empowerment-boosted Cooperative Value Function Interface (EC-VFI), a transfer learning method designed to increase the efficiency of training. Specifically, it enhances the performance of existing policies through modulation of the partner agents' behavior. To capitalize on shared knowledge between related tasks, we've integrated cooperative empowerment, a measure of a policy's ability to coordinate, and weighted the learning objectives according to their contributions. Moreover, we've explored both off-line and on-line tuning of the weighting parameters and employed both types of objectives in a combination of both off-line and on-line settings. We've tested the EC-VFI on a range of cooperative games and the results show the benefits of this approach. To facilitate its use, we've released the EC-VFI's source code at its repository for evaluation.

The significant amount of waste generated from the wrong material being used has prompted industry professionals to seek innovative solutions. Developing a system that can accurately identify materials, especially when the material library is extensive, has become a high priority. Given that one-shot learning can recognize materials under diverse conditions, we leveraged this technique to build a material identification system. Our experimental results show that one-shot learning can successfully apply to both transparent and colored materials, including wraps, films, and surfaces with labels indicating the material type. Furthermore, we explored various image features and discovered that utilizing both local texture features and global visual characteristics yields the best overall material identification performance. Our findings also reveal that material identification can remain effective even when there are differences in material appearance, such as when using multi-color or transparent samples from the same material family. This leads to the development of a semi-supervised material identification system, which can accurately identify materials even with limited data. Our proposed method has the potential to greatly reduce the incorrect material being used, which in turn, results in our estimated reduction of approximately 81% of the incorrect material being used along with a 67% reduction in the number of material samples required for successful material identification.

This paper builds upon previous cohomology theories for Lie 2-algebras developed by Nijhoff and Post, extending it to a more comprehensive framework. Our main objective is to decentralize the initial approach, applying it to a broader range of Lie 2-algebras through decentralization. This led to the realization of two crucial findings: Firstly, the extended cohomology theory preserves key properties analogous to those observed in cohomology theories for ordinary Lie algebras, excluding degree 0. Secondly, degree 1 cohomology is directly tied to the automorphisms of Lie 2-algebras and also facilitates the formal integration of Lie 2-algebras via the 2-cocycle. Lastly, Lie 2-cohomology itself defines a metric on the tangent space of Lie 2-algebras, demonstrating its application in determining the local solvability of 2-plaquettes and Darboux polynomials.

A new approach to identifying features in images has been developed, combining local invariant features with a more robust image descriptor through the use of DeepNet technology. The SIFT alternative, proposed by Bello I and Gonzalez, involves utilizing a DeepNet-based SIFT replacement, featuring a geometrically constrained patch-based image descriptor named PCID. The PCID model, comprising 3D convolutional neural networks, including a constraint module, outperforms traditional SIFT and ORB feature matching techniques. Key findings show that PCID rival SIFT's performance while surpassing ORB. Moreover, PCID outperformed both SIFT and ORB in robustness and precision, particularly in matching features of diverse scales.

Achieving accurate magnetic field assessments from solar vector fields, especially in active regions, remains a challenge due to unresolved fine-scale structures and noise in observations. Often, a standard area-weighted averaging approach is employed, but it fails to account for the underlying magnetic structure, where magnetic fill fraction maps show where structures reside above, below, or across disk normal. We examine the benefit of combining frequency-scaled area-weighting with magnetic fill fraction in vector magnetic field maps. We achieved this by using total intensity data from SOHO/MDI and magnetograph data from Kanzelhoehe Observatory to create synoptic maps, then applied both methods to determine the vector fields. As a result, including fill fraction reduced biases in line-of-sight components, especially in active regions and throughout the disk. Furthermore, including fill fraction minimized the underestimation of flare heights derived from Frejus data and was found to outperform other inversion techniques in this context. We propose that including magnetic fill fraction be standard in vector magnetic field maps and suggest its calculation based on differences between positive and negative magnetic polarity frequencies.

In smart home load management, consumers attempt to maximize their convenience and profit by managing their energy consumption according to flexible power schedules.
We explore a game-theoretic framework where a non-autonomous consumer, referred to as a slave, adheres to a pre-established power schedule negotiated by an autonomous consumer, or a master, seeking personal benefit.
We show through the application of the best and worst-case analysis that the master's ideal time interval for purchasing zero-cost energy is bounded by a specific function.
In scenarios without a slave, this function's lower limit has been extensively studied in literature; however, with a slave in play, this function's upper limit is influenced by the slave's negotiation of power schedules with the electric utility.
We present an efficient negotiation approach in which the slave identifies a feasible power schedule referred to as a β-feasible schedule, which the master can use to achieve a profit within a specified range.
We use mathematical analysis to prove that our approach enables the master to purchase zero-cost energy within a bounded energy balance error.
Notably, the master's energy purchase cost during the power negotiation period is influenced by the slave's energy storage capabilities and negotiation strategy, specifically its β-feasibility, rather than its energy storage efficiency or requirement for zero-cost energy.
Simulations verify our theoretical bounds and compare the performance of the developed strategy against a control approach where the slave and master are autonomous decision-makers.

This paper examines the influence of quantum gravity effects on charged black string stability within the framework of Rastall theory. We establish a differential form approach to the theory's field equations and derive a differential form representation for the Einstein field equations. We then obtain Rastall theory's modified Einstein field equations and apply the theory to charged black string metrics. We analyze the stability of these metrics by studying their singularities and foci in the p vs. q plane under various physical conditions. We compare the stability results with those from quantum corrected charged black string metrics obtained via the Rastall theory Swarup-Debnaray cosmic module.

Building on Ergodic Theorem by von Neumann, we explore averaging operators with dependent coefficients over infinite sequences of time. We extend his findings, showing that convergence rates in non-reversible cases can surpass polynomial rates when the spectral gap is absent. This is demonstrated through a scenario with dependent parameters (p_w(x)) that never repeat, or nearly repeat, across x in an infinite set. Under the assumption that parameters have bounded variation and an ergodic structure, we establish the convergence rates of associated time-averages in (L^p)-spaces over an arbitrary number of dimensions. Our main objective is to characterize the influence of parameters' dependence and ergodic structure on rates of convergence, with the goal of improving current subpolynomial rates for (L^1)-spaces and expanding on prior work by D. Anderson and C. Anderson in related spaces of (L^p) norms with p > 1.

Our research offers a novel method for determining the metallic composition of celestial objects observed in the near-infrared spectrum. In our analysis, we have established a link between relative iron abundance and a specific ratio of light element emission, in the form of $\mbox{[FeI/ISEW]-$\mbox{[CaI/B2F1]}$ (or $\mbox{[FeI/ISEW]-$\mbox{[NaI/B2F1]}$), which serves as an indicator of overall metal content in the atmosphere of these stars. Additionally, our study has identified differences in the behavior of alpha and iron elements as metallicity varies. Based on our new measure, we have recategorized the metal content of HIP124171 as likely to be a subgiant star with a metallicity of around -0.6 to -0.8 times that of the Sun. Furthermore, this new measure has been shown to work effectively for a range of theoretical models representing different atmospheric conditions. It is also effective for determining the metal content of binary systems, including those with non-variable and variable jets of gas flow (microfluid flows). In our work, we have presented various examples of how this measure has been applied in the analysis of different stars.

Global fire data from the MCD19 product (June 2016 - present) was analyzed 
by season and year, utilizing 12 fire seasons from 2016 to 2021. The study 
compared active fire counts, along with their trends, in different regions of 
the world. It found three categories of countries based on fire activity: 
those with a global peak, those without a peak, and those with declining 
fire counts. In the United States, fire counts remained stable, while Europe 
and Asia experienced varying trends, with some having increasing fire counts 
in the far north and decreasing in the south. Three countries analyzed (Australia, 
the US, and Indonesia) showed opposing trends in active fire counts, with Australia 
and the US exhibiting stable fire patterns and Indonesia displaying an increase. 
The analysis also found no correlation between meteorological factors and fire 
data for seven countries, including those with stable or declining fire counts. 
It, however, detected a significant correlation between meteorological factors and 
fire data for nine countries, with a clear relationship between drought and fire 
data for six of these countries.

This research explores the connection between morphological complexity in nouns and typological variables by using a new quantification of morphological complexity based on the length of paradigms rather than traditional measures such as word length or number of phonemes. The study collects data on paradigm length from 50 languages and compares it to various complexity measures and typological variables, such as word order, posession, and basic word order, revealing that paradigm length is correlated with these variables and that its effects are distinct from those of existing complexity measures and syntactic categories. The findings suggest that the quantity of morphs within a noun's paradigm has a substantial and independent impact on the noun's function in sentences and that this complexity measure can explain phenomena not accounted for by previous models.

Research into galaxy clusters' internal structure via a more precise measurement of their gravitational influence in lensing is suggested by current data, which indicates the standard distribution of their dark matter may not accurately represent the gravitational effect in their inner regions. A novel method for quantifying the degree of complexity in a galaxy cluster's substructure uses baryonic content mapping, which could also yield more precise measurements of h100, c_{500} and sigma_v based on lensing data, by approximately 0.6 sigma, 0.4 sigma, 0.6 sigma respectively; whereas previous studies primarily relied on X-ray data, we are exploring a new approach that combines baryonic content maps and multiple lensing data, leading to reduced variability in measurements.

We explore the feasibility of dimensionality reduction for complex mathematical models that have uncertain parameters and are characterized by multiple variables. In specific cases involving elliptic and parabolic equations, we identify the most effective methods for reducing dimensions and observe how these methods can be closely linked with partial differential equations that address optimization problems. The effectiveness of these reduction methods is assessed using rigorous measures and observed outcomes in various numerical experiments. These experiments involve distinct original and target spaces as well as different types of data: randomly selected samples and solutions associated with extreme parameter values. The results suggest that the most suitable reduction method depends on both the type of problem and the available data.

This research introduces a novel approach called m-ar-K function for creating compact representations of data, particularly focusing on multi-dimensional signals. By employing a comprehensive method, the proposed function efficiently discards superfluous data and retains the essential features. The m-ar-K method periodically samples from various angles and masks the data points, ultimately reducing dimensionality. Theoretical analyses demonstrate that m-ar-K based dimensionality reduction yields optimal results, surpassing established techniques like ar-K function. Furthermore, experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets consistently validate the superiority of the proposed method in retaining the crucial information and facilitating efficient feature extraction.

This study presents a spatially aware event detection system that integrates geolocation and temporal data from social media for identifying incidents worldwide. The system overcomes spatial and temporal resolution challenges by using geo-tagged tweets to estimate the occurrence and progression of events in different areas. This allows incidents to be detected and categorized at various scales, from individual streets to broader city areas. Given its versatility, the system can be effectively employed for real-time and large-scale incident monitoring across the globe. Our proposed approach is demonstrated through a case study on traffic congestion in Delhi, India.

This paper delves into the properties of $A$-harmonic functions in nearly starlike domains and incorporates the concept of variational inequalities to formulate free boundary problems for elliptic equations. A key discovery is that $A$-harmonic functions maintain the same homogeneity property as elliptic equations in nearly starlike domains. Building on this characteristic, the paper develops a direct approach to solve the direct problem and establishes a link between the variational inequality and a free boundary problem with an extra simplicity constraint. Furthermore, the authors prove the one-phase solution's stability and continuity up to a phase transition. A key discovery is that the size of the extra domain does not impact the rate of the phase transition at a singular point on the free boundary. This research also touches on the reverse problem, offering an ideal scenario for further exploration. A comprehensive appendix in the paper confirms the relevance of these findings by demonstrating that the Bubnicki-Reed conjecture holds true for nearly starlike domains.

YCo$_x$ compounds with a tetragonal Cmcm structure and a crystalline size of 23-34 nm, produced through high-energy ball-milling methods, exhibit some unique characteristics. These properties include ferromagnetic nature, an increased Curie temperature compared to Y$_2$Co$_{17}$, a temperature at which YCo$_3$ ferromagnetism ceases, and Laves phase element magnetization. The structural and magnetic features of the YCo$_x$ series become similar to Y$_2$Co$_{17}$ as the composition approaches $x=2$. The magnetic and structural characteristics can be explained by the stabilization of a hexagonal close-packed structure in the presence of some divalent and monovalent state Y atoms. The hexagonal structure's energy minimum decreases in comparison to the tetragonal form, indicating that the Y atom valence state impacts the crystal structure stability. The tetragonal structure's magnetic and structural features durability can be attributed to the effects of phonon mechanism in contrast to the hexagonal structure's magnetic and structural features deterioration due to magnetic effects. The YCo$_x$ series ferromagnetic nature disappearance can be ascribed to the hexagonal structure re-appearance, an indication that the hexagonal structure's appearance leads to the Y atom valence state stabilization and the Y$_2$Co$_{17}$ type magnetic characteristics retrieval.
